causes.text: On January 30, 2025, UPS announced plans to shrink Amazon delivery volumes by more than 50%, refocusing on more profitable packages and slashing costs. Reuters reported that UPS was targeting a return to higher-margin business, cutting unprofitable Amazon volumes and reducing billion-dollar overhead. This strategic shift left Amazon searching for other logistics partners and signaled a shakeup in the delivery market.

source_info.title: UPS reducing Amazon delivery volume; shares slump on 2025 revenue hit

effects.text: On May 12, 2025, Amazon hired FedEx to handle some large package deliveries weeks after UPS halted its less-profitable Amazon deliveries. The Reuters article noted that the deal allowed FedEx to carry bulky items to consumers' homes while UPS retrenched. Investors interpreted the deal as a major win for FedEx, and its stock surged about 7% on the day as it captured business that UPS shed.

source_info.title: Amazon signs up FedEx for residential deliveries

causal_reasoning_chain.description: UPS's strategic decision to prioritize profitability over volume led it to cut more than half of its Amazon package deliveries. This shift forced Amazon to seek alternative carriers to maintain service levels.
Amazon, needing to keep delivery promises, turned to FedEx for handling large residential packages. FedEx seized the opportunity to expand its parcel business.
On May 12, 2025, the announcement of the FedEx-Amazon deal drove FedEx shares up about 7%, reflecting investor optimism about revenue growth and network utilization gains.

rationale: UPS's retreat from low-margin Amazon business created a gap that FedEx was able to fill. The subsequent Amazon-FedEx deal illustrates a clear time-lagged causal chain, leading to a sharp positive stock market reaction for FedEx.
counterfactual_analysis: Had UPS not exited much of its Amazon business, Amazon would have had no incentive to sign a new contract with FedEx. In that case, FedEx's residential volume and share price would have remained lower, while UPS's margins would likely have stayed suppressed.

adversarial_confounders.text: Amazon could have renegotiated terms with UPS instead of switching carriers.
adversarial_confounders.impact: This would weaken the causal link between UPS's retreat and FedEx's stock surge.
Broader demand could have lifted FedEx shares regardless of the Amazon contract.

details.commentary: UPS's decision to walk away from low-margin Amazon volumes reshuffled rivalry dynamics in parcel delivery. The move opened space for FedEx to capture lucrative large-package flows, strengthening its competitive position against both UPS and Amazon Logistics.

Underlying e-commerce growth kept overall parcel demand robust even as carriers shifted their mix toward more profitable freight. In that environment, the ability to redeploy capacity from a retrenching rival made FedEx's new deal with Amazon look especially attractive to investors.

Once UPS stepped back, FedEx could add Amazon volumes that improved stop density and asset utilization across its network. Better economics supported earnings expectations, and the stock's sharp move higher in turn validated management's strategy, encouraging further pursuit of similar business.
